title: AlphaMissense: cataloging missense genetic mutations
summary: It classified 89% of the 71 million possible missense variants: 32% as likely pathogenic and 57% as likely benign, with 90% precision on a database of known variants. Predictions are not intended for direct clinical use.

evidence.tested: The model was validated on genetic and experimental benchmarks, and Genomics England cross-referenced its predictions with previously aggregated human variant pathogenicity data and found them consistent.
evidence.unknown: The model does not predict structural or stability effects, the blog says predictions are not designed for direct clinical use, and the abstract describes no clinical validation.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaMissense, an AlphaFold adaptation fine-tuned on human and primate variant population frequency data, classified missense variants and released predictions for all possible human substitutions.
